about.title: Lakeport Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Lakeport's small size doesn't mean its workforce is exempt from job-site injuries — whether at a local business along Main Street, a construction site, or a service job that requires driving through town. In California, workers' compensation is generally the only path against your own employer, no matter who was at fault. But if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party. Lake County workers navigating these overlapping systems often benefit from guidance that keeps both timelines in view: report the injury to your employer within 30 days, and remember that any third-party civil claim carries its own two-year deadline. Our team helps injured workers in Lakeport understand which path, or paths, apply to their situation, free of charge.

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only claim against your employer, but that doesn't close every door. We can evaluate whether a third party's negligence opened a separate path to recovery.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting a workplace injury. If you're worried about your job while healing, we can help you understand your rights.

items.title: Two Clocks, Two Deadlines
items.desc: Reporting an injury to your employer within 30 days is critical, but a third-party civil claim runs on a separate two-year deadline. Missing either one can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt at work in Lakeport — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault. However, if a third party — like a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate civil claim. We can help sort out which applies to your situation.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Main Street or 11th Street?
items.answer: If you were injured in a vehicle collision while performing work duties on Lakeport corridors like Main Street or 11th Street, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a potential third-party claim against another driver. These situations often involve more moving parts, so getting guidance early can help protect your options.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report workplace injuries or file workers' compensation claims. If you believe you've faced retaliation, we can help you understand what protections apply. Contact us at no upfront cost.
